source: derived from the clause 4.1.3 field layout
note: The 6-octet Space Packet primary header. Field layout from clause 4.1.3: version 3 bits, type 1 bit, secondary header flag 1 bit, APID 11 bits, sequence flags 2 bits, sequence count 14 bits, then the 16-bit packet data length. Each vector below isolates one field so a packing error names itself instead of hiding in a full packet.

encode.name: sequence-flag-continuation
encode.note: Sequence flags '00' means a continuation segment. byte 2 = 00<<6 | (count>>8) = 0x00 with count 1, byte 3 = 0x01.

encode.name: sequence-flag-first-segment
encode.note: Sequence flags '01' means the first segment. byte 2 = 01<<6 = 0x40 with count 1 in the low 14 bits.

encode.name: sequence-flag-last-segment
encode.note: Sequence flags '10' means the last segment. byte 2 = 10<<6 = 0x80.

encode.name: sequence-flag-unsegmented
encode.note: Sequence flags '11' means unsegmented, a standalone packet. byte 2 = 11<<6 = 0xc0. This is the common case and the default every other vector here uses.

encode.name: packet-type-tm
encode.note: The packet type bit is bit 4 of byte 0 and is 0 for telemetry. With APID 0x123: byte 0 = 000<<5 | 0<<4 | 0<<3 | 0x123>>8 = 0x01, byte 1 = 0x23.

encode.name: packet-type-tc
encode.note: The same APID with the type bit set for telecommand: byte 0 = 0<<5 | 1<<4 | 0<<3 | 0x123>>8 = 0x11. Only bit 4 differs from packet-type-tm, which is the point of the pair.

encode.name: secondary-header-flag-clear
encode.note: The secondary header flag is bit 3 of byte 0. Clear with APID 100: byte 0 = 0x00.

encode.name: secondary-header-flag-set
encode.note: The same header with the flag set: byte 0 = 1<<3 | 0x064>>8 = 0x08. Only bit 3 differs from secondary-header-flag-clear.

encode.name: apid-zero
encode.note: The APID is the low 11 bits of the first two octets. Zero gives bytes 0-1 = 00 00.

encode.name: apid-all-ones-is-idle
encode.note: APID 'all ones' (0x7ff, 2047) is reserved for idle packets. Bytes 0-1 = 07 ff. This is the largest value the 11-bit field holds, so it also pins the field width.

encode.name: apid-alternating-bits
encode.note: APID 0x2aa alternates bits across the octet boundary, so a shift error shows up. byte 0 = 0x2aa>>8 = 0x02, byte 1 = 0x2aa&0xff = 0xaa.

encode.name: sequence-count-zero
encode.note: The sequence count is the low 14 bits of octets 2-3. Zero with unsegmented flags gives bytes 2-3 = c0 00.

encode.name: sequence-count-max
encode.note: 16383 is the largest value 14 bits hold. With unsegmented flags: bytes 2-3 = 11<<14 | 0x3fff = 0xffff. A count that overflowed into the flag bits would be indistinguishable from this, which is why the maximum is pinned.

encode.name: packet-length-one-octet-data-field
encode.note: The packet data length field carries the data field size minus one, so the smallest legal data field of one octet gives a length field of zero. Bytes 4-5 = 00 00.

encode.name: packet-length-max
encode.note: A length field of 0xffff means a data field of 65536 octets, the largest the standard allows. Bytes 4-5 = ff ff.

decode.name: all-fields-at-once
decode.note: One header with every field set to a distinct non-default value, so a decoder that reads two fields from the same bits fails here. version 0, type 1 (TC), secondary header flag 1, APID 0x2aa, sequence flags '10' (last segment), count 0x1234, length 0x00ff. byte 0 = 0<<5|1<<4|1<<3|0x02 = 0x1a, byte 1 = 0xaa, byte 2 = 10<<6|0x12 = 0x92, byte 3 = 0x34, bytes 4-5 = 00 ff.

reject.name: header-truncated-to-five-octets
reject.note: The primary header is always exactly six octets, so five cannot hold it.
